# dotfiles — an agent's map

> One person's macOS daily driver: nushell + tmux + WezTerm + nvim +
> television, deployed by a 60-line sh script that copies home/ over
> $HOME. No manager, no templates, no gates. Read the file that matches
> what you are about to touch, in the same change you touch it.

These files explain how everything works. They live in docs/llms/ and
are searched, together with the manual, by `?` in the shell.

## Start here

- [deploy.txt](docs/llms/deploy.txt) — dotfiles.sh, install.sh, hooks/,
  removed.txt retirement, rr, the Brewfile. How the repo becomes the
  machine.
- [conventions.txt](docs/llms/conventions.txt) — how to work in this
  repo: subtraction over machinery, TRAP comments, the pickers rule,
  retirement, the manual.
- [decisions.txt](docs/llms/decisions.txt) — the dated decision record:
  what was chosen, why, what it beat.

## Subsystems

- [shell.txt](docs/llms/shell.txt) — nushell: env repair, config anchors,
  the prompt and its caches (prompt.nu, gitseg.nu), the one navigation
  funnel, keys, finder/quicklist/help, state files.
- [tmux.txt](docs/llms/tmux.txt) — multiplexing, the F5 cockpit and its
  frame cache, zen mode, the ~/.local/bin scripts.
- [terminal.txt](docs/llms/terminal.txt) — WezTerm chrome, tinty palette
  ownership, television channels and cable files.
- [nvim.txt](docs/llms/nvim.txt) — lazy.nvim layout, plugins, the
  editor-side constraints.
- [capsule.txt](docs/llms/capsule.txt) — the one container tool:
  image hash, credential refresh, the scripts.
- [machines.txt](docs/llms/machines.txt) — provisioning order, secrets at
  runtime, remote access over the tailnet, host traps.

## The user-facing manual

The shell's `?` and `help` read the manual shipped in
home/.config/nushell/help/ — the .nuon surfaces are the source of truth
for commands and keys (`just manual` regenerates the guide and reference
halves); internals/ is hand-written system detail that these files point
into rather than repeat.

## Keeping this true

Update the txt in the same commit as the behavior change. A stale file
here is worse than no file: an agent that trusts it will rebuild the
system wrong.
